title: Coincidence free certification and quantification of spatial entanglement with stimulated parametric down conversion
authors: M. G. Damaceno, G. H. dos Santos, N. Rubiano da Silva, S. P. Walborn, P. H. Souto Ribeiro
abstract: Using stimulated emission, a photon pair source can be characterized by seeding the signal mode with a bright classical beam and measuring the stimulated idler field, thus replacing two-photon coincidence counting with classical intensity detection. We apply this approach to the continuous transverse spatial degrees of freedom of a down conversion source and show that it is possible to certify spatial entanglement with only intensity measurements. We demonstrate this capability through variance-based entanglement and steering witnesses, as well as the Fedorov ratio. This method is useful for studying entanglement properties of photon pair sources in conditions where alignment and photon counting measurements are difficult and time-consuming.
summary: This paper details a novel technique to certify and quantify spatial entanglement in photon pairs generated by SPDC. By employing stimulated parametric down conversion (StimPDC), the authors replace slow coincidence counting with simple intensity measurements on the idler beam. This method successfully verifies entanglement using established witnesses, proving its utility for quantum optics experiments where precise photon detection is challenging.
main_problem: The core problem is certifying and quantifying spatial entanglement of photon pairs generated by SPDC without relying on slow, coincidence-counting measurements.
main_result: Spatial entanglement and EPR steering can be robustly certified using only intensity measurements from the idler beam via stimulated parametric down conversion (StimPDC).
method: The authors use StimPDC by seeding the signal mode with a bright classical beam, allowing them to measure conditional idler states using standard intensity detectors instead of coincidence counting.
model_or_system: The system involves entangled photon pairs generated via SPDC. The measurement technique utilizes stimulated emission into the idler field, which is then analyzed in both transverse position and momentum bases.
key_observables: Entanglement witnesses (Reid criterion, MGVT product) and the Fedorov ratio ($R$), calculated from measured conditional variances ($\sigma^2$).
important_parameters: The correlation strength is tracked by varying the pump waist size; finite seed widths only broaden measured variances.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes paraxial and quasi-monochromatic approximations, and the method's robustness relies on imperfections only broadening measurements, preventing false positives.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate conceptual diagrams for position-space and momentum-space seeding (Fig. 1). Other figures show measured near-field/far-field intensity profiles and correlation plots confirming expected linear fits.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the StimPDC method to replace coincidence counting, derives the conditional idler state, applies entanglement witnesses (Reid, MGVT), calculates the Fedorov ratio, and presents results demonstrating robust certification of spatial entanglement using only intensity measurements.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly practical experimental protocol for quantum optics that bypasses major technical hurdles in quantum measurement, making entanglement characterization accessible under difficult experimental conditions.
